title: Cover
description: Title slide for the Practitioner Operating Plan — the team and budget that make the yes sustainable.

title: Why this matters
description: Naming the contract as the inflection point and the question it forces — what does the yes have to look like to stay a yes?

title: Bright Side is the highway
description: Part I opener — names Bright Side (the PHI-free residential-care staff companion app, Zone 0 centralized, paired with SaltBox) as the life focus and the highway every other line either feeds or stays out of.

title: Three doors, one product
description: Three doors into Bright Side, all already shipped: the floor (/unit-sheet clipboard with transition runs), the lobby (/lobby MVP wall + yesterday strip), and the director (/sector templates + planning pages). One codebase, three audiences.

title: The line I won't lose
description: The mission line: the institution can be a cultivated microclimate, not a wind tunnel — every screen a small wall against the wind. Names the four teachers (TSP, Salatin, LFTN, Cells) and how each shows up in the product.

title: Why I haven't started yet — and what ends that
description: Names the loose-ends trap, commits to working backwards from the next conference date toward a Princess Court (or other Kenora-district) pilot, and gives permission to start before the desk is clean.

title: Part II — What Headwaters is
description: Section divider introducing the agency container: vision, name, and the brand & IP runway.

title: Agency vision
description: How this contract is the foundation — months 1–6, 6–12, and the year 2–3 picture of a small consultancy carrying multiple northern community contracts. Bridges into Part VII (the template).

title: Naming the agency: Headwaters
description: The inflection point — the dam-breaks framing, the brand structure (Headwaters parent → Watershed product + Deer Lake pilot + future engagements), and the one-line rationale that Headwaters has the open lanes while Watershed has the contested ones.

title: Brand & IP landscape
description: Domains available vs. taken (WHOIS Apr 2026) and the indicative trademark picture for Watershed (191 marks, contested in Class 9/36) vs. Headwaters (76 marks, no active mark in Class 36 financial services or Class 9 consumer software).

title: Part III — What I protect
description: Section divider entering the protection layer: non-negotiables, daily and weekly rhythm, what a great week looks like, and the two hard rules that keep the bet alive.

title: The non-negotiables
description: Five things that don't move: phone-free until 10am, 7–10am with the kids, work block 10:30 to 4/6, dinner already prepared, weekends mostly off.

title: Daily rhythm — summer vs winter
description: Side-by-side daily rhythm for summer and winter, because winter is the part that breaks plans.

title: Weekly rhythm and check-ins
description: The 11am and 4pm hand-offs with the on-site Dryden manager and the optional weekend deep-work block.

title: What a great week looks like
description: A narrative slide reflecting the practitioner's own words back to them — three tests for whether the week was actually good.

title: Two hard rules
description: The two non-negotiables that govern the legacy lines under Headwaters: founder's hands off jars and tables forever, and Deer Lake gets first call on the shared team's hours. Quarterly hours-by-pillar check enforces it.

title: Part IV — The pipeline I keep
description: Section divider for the pipeline discipline: the rule, the prospect map, the one-SaaS focus, the shiny-loose-end test, and the recurring founder action items.

title: No contract closes without the next one named
description: The hard rule — every closing engagement requires a named next contract before sign-off. Voiced in the same register as the non-negotiables and the two hard rules.

title: Prospect map
description: 807 Food, Parr's Jars, Bright Side, Headwaters Finance (Enthusiast / Credit Union / IG), Headwaters Governance, Start9 + Privacy Phones — each graded Floor / Highway / Long game and tagged for whether it respects or threatens the non-negotiables.

title: One SaaS at a time
description: Bright Side is the bet now; Headwaters Finance Credit Union is named-target only when warm; Enthusiast tier is community marketing, not a second product launch.

title: The shiny loose end test
description: Four questions before saying yes to anything new: does it ladder to the mission line, does it cost work-block hours, is the next contract named, and does Bright Side advance this week regardless?

title: What the founder does this week
description: Sequenced personal-action checklist with registrar/registry links and costs: domains today, defensive registrations, CIPO trademark search, Google Workspace email, paid agent clearance opinion, and NUANS search before incorporating. The recurring action page for Part IV.

title: Part V — Deer Lake — the contract that pays
description: Section divider entering the operating voice for the current contract: six roles, seven hires, one budget, and the accountability bar.

title: Operations Manager (Dryden)
description: The phone-holder and time-protector, on-site in Dryden, dual-purpose for 807 ops and Deer Lake aggregation/distribution. 40 hrs/wk @ $40/hr ≈ $7,000/mo.

title: Bookkeeper / Agency Admin
description: Invoicing, contracts, CRA, the back office of the agency — built once, used for years. 10 hrs/wk @ $40/hr ≈ $1,700/mo.

title: Food Handler (embedded at the Deer Lake store)
description: Headwaters-owned Food Handler embedded at the Deer Lake store from Day 1: salt batches, 807-branded piecework, kitchen + shop tidy, food/supplies inventory.

title: Housecleaner
description: Recurring weekly clean — the mid-week mess reset taken off the parent and put on the schedule. 4 hrs/wk @ $30/hr ≈ $500/mo.

title: Tutor
description: Math, reading, structure — winter-weighted (~10 hrs/wk Nov–Apr, ~2 hrs/wk in summer). ≈ $900/mo annualised.

title: Handyman-Housekeeper combo
description: Practical-first, parenting-intent second, framed as 'consider, don't commit' with explicit vetting requirements. 5 hrs/wk @ $30/hr ≈ $700/mo if engaged.

title: Part V — Hiring runbook
description: Sub-divider inside Part V for the hiring runbook: how to actually find each agency hire and household support, with sourcing channels in and around Dryden, screening questions, paid trial structures, and walk-away signals.

title: Hiring — Operations Manager
description: How to find the Dryden ops manager: Chamber and Job Bank, Confederation College alumni, regional logistics referrals, Facebook groups, bulletin boards. Screening questions, 2-week paid shadow-then-solo trial, walk-away signals, 30/60/90.

title: Hiring — Bookkeeper
description: How to find the bookkeeper: CPB Canada directory, Northwestern Ontario CPAs, Chamber referrals, Indeed/LinkedIn remote-Canada search. Screening on CRA fluency, 1-month paid trial against fixed scope, walk-away signals, 30/60/90.

title: Hiring — IT/Tech
description: Hiring runbook for the IT/Tech role: source from northern-Ontario MSPs and self-hosting communities, screen for runbook discipline, paid one-week trial.

title: Hiring — Food Handler
description: Hiring runbook for the Headwaters-owned Food Handler at the Deer Lake store: source from Deer Lake first, screen for kitchen + cleaning fit, paid two-shift trial.

title: Hiring — Housecleaner
description: How to find the weekly housecleaner: working-parent referrals first, Dryden Facebook groups and Kijiji second, bulletin boards, Molly Maid as paid backstop. Screening, 2-visit paid trial, walk-away signals, 30/60/90.

title: Hiring — Tutor
description: How to find the year-round tutor: Lakehead Faculty of Education, Confederation College EA program, Keewatin-Patricia DSB, Dryden retired teachers, OCT register, current-teacher referrals. Vulnerable Sector Check required, 4-session paid trial with kids voting, 30/60/90.

title: Hiring — Handyman-Housekeeper
description: How to find the handyman-housekeeper safely: referrals only, never an open posting. Explicit child-safety vetting protocol — Vulnerable Sector Check, three reference calls, never alone with kids for 90 days, open conversation with the kids, annual re-check. Two-week paid trial outside-then-inside-with-parent-present, heavy walk-away list, slower 30/60/90.

title: Budget — three contract sizes (cost × 1.35)
description: Cost-basis composition with new $60k/$90k/$125k contract sizes. Bill = cost × 1.35; the 35% is a dedicated reinvestment line.

title: Cash flow — bridging the 60-day pay cycle
description: 12-month cumulative cash chart for all three contract sizes including day-one tech CAPEX and the new aggregation hub line, naming the bridge capital required (~$95k / $181k / $251k) before the first invoice clears.

title: The $22k already spent — how we get paid back
description: Names the $22,000 owed to Headwaters for the full 807 grant deliverable scope — both the CDP/business-development stream and the marketing/promotion stream the other contractor backed out of — plus Replit hosting actuals, framed as ~$40k of original grant scope delivered for $22k. Proposes a two-trigger repayment structure (deficit clears OR new platform-enabled revenue starts producing) with no cash up front, no debt taken on by 807, and no draw on existing operations until a trigger is met. Footer links to /payback-memo, the printable signed memorandum that turns the slide into a paper trail both organisations can hold each other to.

title: Reinvestment — what the 35% builds
description: Four destinations of the 35% markup: tech CAPEX (~$60k/yr — 9 servers, 6 privacy phones, computers), tooling subscriptions (~$2k/mo), training & R&D (~$3k/mo), and the pilot scale reserve (~$10k/mo accruing).

title: Net-positive accountability
description: Five measures (procurement savings delivered, time returned to band staff, transparency tooling shipped & adopted, capacity built locally, year-end value-delivered audit) plus a forward-credit clause if the value delivered doesn't beat the markup.

title: Part VI — For Dad
description: Section divider entering the contractor voice — the case for the rate, the case for the team, value delivered, naming the deal, and the next two weeks.

title: The case for the rate
description: What $90k/month actually buys — operating system, transparency stack, and pilot reserve — versus what 'lean' actually costs (the contract and the next reserve waiting in line).

title: The case for the team
description: Single-point-of-failure 'lean' versus the structured team — saves $11k on paper / costs the contract, vs. costs $11k / buys the contract and the next one.

title: Value delivered
description: Four deliverables for the rate: optimized food-price model, winter delivery execution, transparency stack + infrastructure that scales, and base stability.

title: Naming the deal
description: Slide that names the deal in Dad's language — 'no free lunches, capital deployed properly, value out the other end' — at $90k/mo on a 12-month engagement reviewed at month six, with ~$181k bridge ask.

title: The next two weeks
description: A two-week feedback and negotiating window between handing the deck over and naming the deal: opens Mon Apr 27, 2026 and closes when the contractor is back home from Deer Lake (~Sun May 10 / Mon May 11). Three beats — Week 1 read & react on the road, Week 2 talk it through, Closing day name the deal at the kitchen table — plus the founder posture that no guided execution work begins until the deal is named.

title: Part VII — Pilot to template
description: Section divider entering the scale voice: Deer Lake earns it, then so does every reserve. The template the practitioner builds for pilot #1 is the playbook the next reserve inherits.

title: Why Deer Lake is Pilot #1
description: Three reasons Deer Lake is the right pilot: the right scale (~870 people), a council ready for transparency, and a practitioner with skin in the game and the structural plan to deliver.

title: The six-module template
description: What gets templatized: operating plan, hiring runbook, financial model, transparency stack, tech infrastructure, net-positive accountability. Each module is documented as we ship it for Deer Lake.

title: The path to scale
description: Five-year arc: Year 1 Deer Lake pilot, Year 2 second reserve at marginal cost, Year 3 three-to-five concurrent contracts, Year 5 open template that any practitioner can run.

title: Part VIII — What outlives the contract
description: Section divider entering the legacy lines under Headwaters: salt and design under the parent, plus the winter contingency that has to survive every year.

title: Salt under Headwaters
description: Parr's Jars stays — but as a shared-depot revenue line, not a DTC jar-packing or farmers-market business. Three roles under Headwaters (proof of model, depot load-test, shared-labor revenue), with DTC moving to batch-only and markets sunset.

title: Salt runbook — through the Dryden depot
description: How the salt line actually runs: monthly batch cadence in the last week of each month, channel-by-channel inventory rules (6-week wholesale buffer, custom-labels paid up front, zero standing DTC stock), the day-by-day Mon→Fri week of the batch with ops-manager hours and casual-labour share, returns routing, and explicit drop-rules when a Deer Lake aggregation run lands the same week. Rules 01 and 02 enforced inline.

title: Salt Klaviyo flow — batch slip + batch shipped
description: The two customer emails the salt runbook promises, drafted and wired in Klaviyo: a manual-trigger 'your batch ships [date]' slip notice fired by the OM when a Deer Lake aggregation run pushes the DTC batch a week, and an auto-fired monthly 'your batch shipped' notification on the Shippo label webhook. Includes subject + preheader + body copy, trigger conditions, audience segments, cadence rules, the Shopify metafield as the date source of truth, and the seed-list test gate before promoting to live.

title: Salt storefront — checkout & dynamic batch date
description: Storefront mockup for parrsjars.ca showing the dynamic next-batch-ship date in three places: sitewide banner, cart drawer line, and the order confirmation. Documents the Shopify metafield → theme → Klaviyo catalog sync chain, the explicitly banned copy ('ships in 2 days', 'in stock — order now', countdown timers), and the metafield-empty fallback that keeps the storefront safe with a Slack ping to the OM.

title: OM operator note — slip flow & next batch date
description: One-page operator note for the Dryden ops manager covering when to fire the slip flow (Wed 11:00–14:00 trigger window, four-step checklist) and how to set the next batch date (recurring first-Mon 9:00 ET, four-step checklist), plus the five-don't list signed at OM onboarding. Pinned in Notion and posted on the depot wall next to the salt runbook.

title: Depot casual-labour bench
description: The named, pre-vetted 4-person Dryden-area casual-labour bench the salt runbook leans on so Rule 01 holds. Seed roster (4 named members with bases, vetting notes, availability windows, and rotation slots), a written A→B→C→D rotation policy with paid standby, the bench cost broken out as a $15k/yr SALT-01-LBR cost-centre that ties back to the salt P&L, an OM runbook for adding/screening/paperwork (T4A + WSIB), and the explicit T-7/T-3/T-0/T+7 batch-slips path for the week the whole bench is unavailable.

title: Salt P&L line
description: Annual P&L for the salt line by channel (wholesale, custom labels, DTC batch, sunset markets) — revenue, COGS, freight, packaging, allocated labour share, gross margin per channel, and the depot rent allocation. Net contribution sized against the recommended $90k/mo agency ask, with the explicit triggers that cut a channel.

title: Design under Headwaters
description: Outside studio intake closes; design becomes the in-house Transparency Stack delivered inside community-development engagements. Two narrow carve-outs: mission-aligned regional work that's really Pilot #2 in disguise, and the studio site staying live as portfolio.

title: Winter contingency
description: What scales up, what gets dropped without guilt, and what stays exactly the same when the kids are stuck inside.

title: Re-read this when you're tired
description: Single closing page restating the bet, the non-negotiables in one line, the pipeline rule, and the mission line — the deck in one place when the head needs reset.
